newsitem.title: TAIWAN: POLL-Taiwan July trade surplus seen down 49 pct.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Taiwan July trade surplus seen down 49 pct.

text.p: A Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists on Tuesday projected a US$686 million trade surplus in Taiwan for July, down 49 percent compared to a July 1996 surplus of US$1.345 billion.
The economists projected July exports rising a year-on-year average 9.22 percent and imports rising 18.86 percent.
Official figures were to be issued by the Finance Ministry at 0245 GMT on August 7.

June showed a trade surplus of US$321.9 million, a 21.5 percent year-on-year decline, with exports at US$9.959 billion and imports at US$9.638 billion.
In July 1996, exports were US$9.464 billion and imports were US$8.119 billion, giving a trade surplus of US$1.345 billion.
Economists attributed the double-digit July imports growth forecast to a low base in July 1996 and a surge of military imports in July 1997.
"Imports of military equipment such as warplanes should contribute most to July's import growth," said HSBC James Capel economist Stephen Wang.
In early July, Taiwan took delivery of a five French-made Mirage 2000 warplanes as part of moves to strengthen itself in the face of rival China's military modernisation.
Taiwan has ordered 60 Mirage and 150 U.S. F-16 fighters.
Economists said the island's booming stock market, whose index has surged more than 45 percent so far in 1997, should boost imports of consumer goods.

"Imports of consumer goods should increase largely as people have earned money from the red-hot stock market, but the impact so far has not been significant," said Grand Cathay Securities economist Chang Jui-hsing.
The Taiwan dollar's sharp late July depreciation would help Taiwan's export competitiveness, though it could slow imports, economists said.
"The sharp Taiwan dollar depreciation should help our export competitiveness, but the impact won't be major until August," said Nomura Securities economist Amy Huang.
The Taiwan dollar had depreciated to an eight-year closing low of T$28.752 on August 1 against the greenback from T$27.92 in late July, T$27.66 in early May and T$27.34 in mid-January.
Most economists said they expected a strong third-quarter recovery for the information and electronics exports, which would help boost overall export performance.
